_README: A RECIPE IS A SET OF WAGES. The bot learns to do whatever you pay it for,
and nothing else. Each number says 'how many fitness points is one of these
worth'. Negative numbers are fines. Everything is per match, per player.
PREFER THE *Diff TERMS. 'I got 30 last hits' is a bad goal — in a long match
everyone gets 30. 'I got 12 MORE last hits than my opponent' is a real one.
Paying for the gap also takes match length out of the equation. An earlier
version of these recipes paid for totals, and evolution promptly discovered
that the safest way to win was to hide behind its own creeps and farm
quietly until the clock ran out. The differentials fixed that.
win/loss/draw  flat payout for the match result
speed          bonus for winning FAST (and mercy for losing slowly)
csDiff         per last-hit MORE than the opponent      <- use these
killDiff       per net kill                             <-
goldDiff       per gold of net worth lead (~0.02)       <-
lvlDiff        per level of lead                        <-
dmgDiff        per point of hero-damage lead (~0.02)    <-
denyDiff       per net deny                             <-
towerDiff      per point of tower-damage lead           <-
cs deny gold level csRate kill assist death dmgHero towerDmg heal
the same things as absolute totals — use sparingly
aggression     per unit of average lane position (0 = own tower, 1 = theirs)
passivity      paid on the fraction of time spent farming/retreating —
make it NEGATIVE to discourage stalling
variety        rewards a spread of behaviours instead of one on repeat
Add your own by copying a block and renaming it, then:
node train.js --recipe myrecipe
node versus.js --a myrecipe --b balanced

farmer.desc: Greedy economist. Wins by out-levelling you, avoids fights it doesn't need.

brawler.desc: Wants your blood. Trades constantly, dives towers, ignores the wave.

sieger.desc: Doesn't care about you at all. Shoves the wave and takes the tower.

survivor.desc: Allergic to dying. Punishing to kill, slowly grinds you out.

purewin.desc: Paid for one thing only: winning. The purest signal, and by far the slowest to learn — a good experiment once the others work.
